note_on_prior_verdict: A prior verdict-02.json existed and is overwritten here. It ruled the equipment-art keys (photography/science/sewing/singing/swimming/skating/skiing/scuba-diving/soccer) as METONYMS - 'the row's word is Singen, not Mikrofon' - and classified them from the LABEL. That is the exact reasoning the brief rejects: its chess example has themes [activities, toys] and the same shape, and the brief rules it countable-thing + LEMMA MISMATCH, calling the metonym/abstract reading wrong. I opened every image and rule from the picture. BUT the prior pass earned two changes to my draft on checkable evidence: (1) tennis/table-tennis are two-object emblems of a sport, and Duden gives 'das Tennis; Genitiv: des Tennis' with NO plural - a real neuter gender that 'activity' would strip, so they are abstract, not activity; (2) it caught an fr gender bug on 'mercury' that I had missed. Its sibling-key claims (soccer-ball, tennis-ball, tennis-racket exist; no volleyball-ball) I verified in image-vocabulary.js and they are all true.
systemic_finding: THE 'activities' THEME PAIRS ACTIVITY-LABELS WITH EQUIPMENT-ART. Eight keys share one root cause: photography=a camera, science=a microscope, sewing=a sewing machine, singing=a microphone, swimming=goggles, skating=one ice skate, skiing=a pair of skis, scuba-diving=a mask+snorkel. Not one of these pictures shows the action; reading/running/writing/sledding/snowboarding in the same domain DO. SEQUENCING HAZARD the operator must see: for these keys my hasPlural:true describes the pictured OBJECT (Mikrofon->Mikrofone). It must NOT be applied to the CURRENT label - pluralising 'Singen' or 'Schwimmen' would manufacture exactly the garbage this commission exists to delete. Fix the LEMMA MISMATCH first (correct the label to the object word, or replace the art with an action drawing), then apply the flag. Which of those two fixes is right is an operator content call, not mine.
